summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a complex medical history including stem cell transplant status, chronic systolic heart failure, chronic kidney disease stage 5, and prior graft-versus-host disease, was admitted for evaluation of progressive shortness of breath and profound weakness. He presented with presyncope and was found to have acute posthemorrhagic anemia, with hemoglobin dropping from 12.8 to 7.8 g/dL, and a history of black stools. He had recently been on high-dose steroids for worsening cardiomyopathy, which likely contributed to upper gastrointestinal bleeding. He received one unit of packed red blood cells and underwent an EGD and colonoscopy, which revealed gastritis and patchy colonic erythema, raising concern for possible gut graft-versus-host disease. He was managed with IV then oral proton-pump inhibition, held on aspirin, and tapered back to baseline prednisone. His hemoglobin stabilized, and he was discharged home with services, on increased torsemide, with follow-up arranged in gastroenterology, cardiology, and nephrology.
